title: Phase 2: complete the newsroom CMS (publish step, Markdown importer, article editing in the Shadcn newsroom app, rebuild-on-publish)

comments.author: home
comments.text:
PHASE 2 PLAN (written 2026-10-05 from origin/develop a10609d, docs/standard-site.md, spike PPY-82be6c / PR #100, epic PPY-1f1489 comments). 19 sub-tasks (kbs allows only `sub-task` under a `task`), label `phase-2`, each fully specified for a separate implementer agent (files, functions, data shapes, tests, acceptance commands, risks, what needs Ryan). Nothing is implemented.

TICKETS (id, one line, estimate = rough working days for an implementer agent)
PPY-78e818 (3d) Semantic Release + npm/PyPI trusted publishing for @anthusai/papyrus + papyrus-newsroom, package smoke checks (compiled backend entry, npm ci --dry-run, wheel import), Ryan's click-by-click registry steps.
PPY-302a5f (1d) Fix the 3 failing JS suites (forum routes, theme-packs, card-layout) and add tests.yml as the CI gate.
PPY-672ea6 (2d) Brand registration from the publication repo: brands out of lib/site-brand.ts into papyrus.config.ts, brand slots for TI-only components, drop ?brand= cookie and alias table, theme CSS via alias, tarball has zero publications/*.
PPY-44a0f9 (1d) Add bodyMarkus, bodyIr, aliases, metadata to Item and PublishedItem (schema.ts AND the duplicate in resource.ts, Python field lists, TS types, parity test).
PPY-e169c5 (2.5d) derive_body(): Papyrus markup lowering + in-process Markus 0.5.1 -> validated bodyIr envelope with error codes; `papyrus content markus-derive`.
PPY-b3a10e (2.5d) save_item / publish_item / unpublish_item (Item -> PublishedItem + media), versionNumber per publish, `papyrus content publish|unpublish`, shared FakeAuthoringClient.
PPY-3e5235 (2.5d) Python Lambda papyrus-content-actions: GraphQL deriveMarkus, saveItemDraft, publishItem, unpublishItem (editor/admin) + TS client.
PPY-22a3b4 (3d) `papyrus content import-markus`: Git Markus dir -> Items + MediaAsset + S3, aliases, drafts, idempotent, never overwrites CMS edits, validates all before writing.
PPY-1d0f3d (2d) `papyrus content export-published [--drafts]`: CMS -> Markus build input dir (+ manifest, redirects.json), fail-closed on empty; round-trip check script and test.
PPY-cddfb8 (2.5d) Pretext reads bodyIr (lib/markus-body.ts), `papyrus content convert-bodies` for legacy body[], seeds write Markus, TS seed stops seeding articles.
PPY-3e5e9d (3d) Staging for Pretext: PAPYRUS_CONTENT_SOURCE=drafts (Item models via userPool cookies, uncached), editor/admin gate in middleware, SITE_ENV guards (noindex, robots, banner), identityPool for published / userPool for drafts.
PPY-f00c89 (2d) Staging for Markus-static: private preview/ S3 prefix served by a gated Next route with the viewer's own Cognito credentials; `papyrus content upload-preview`.
PPY-8ef4ca (4d) /newsroom/articles list + Markus editor (YAML + body textareas, live validation with line numbers, structural preview, Save/Publish/Unpublish) + Gherkin in demo mode.
PPY-ad5ca4 (1.5d) Editor image upload (S3 + MediaAsset + ::image{} insertion, real image in preview).
PPY-39f928 (4d) infra/site.json-driven app shell: no PAT, CMS prod+staging branches, optional reader app, generated build specs on published packages with Python 3.12, synth tests.
PPY-e7f81e (1.5d) GitHub OIDC provider (once per account) + per-site CI role + runbook (GitHub App connection per app).
PPY-fbb1fb (1.5d) Rebuild-on-publish: Amplify StartJob (IAM, no webhook URL/token) for reader, Pretext revalidation, on-demand staging rebuild.
PPY-085f79 (4d) VideoML Python pipeline moved from TI main into papyrus_content/videoml, publication-supplied video config, `papyrus videos` generic.
PPY-961956 (3d) VideoML browser side: article-video, video-mode/script helpers, bundle builders, brand.video slot.
Total about 46.5 agent-days; critical path about 13 days with parallel agents (SCH/DER -> PUB -> LMB -> UIL -> UIM).

DEPENDENCIES (kbs blocked-by): BRD<-CIT; PUB<-DER,SCH; LMB<-SCH,DER,PUB; IMP<-DER,PUB,SCH; EXP<-PUB,DER,SCH; PRT<-SCH,DER; PRV<-PRT,BRD; STG<-PRV,EXP; UIL<-LMB,PUB,DER; UIM<-UIL,IMP; INF<-REL; OIC<-INF,REL; RBP<-LMB,PUB,INF,STG; VID1<-REL,BRD; VID2<-BRD,REL. (relates-to: EXP~IMP, INF~PRV/STG, VID1~VID2/IMP/EXP, CIT~REL.)

EXECUTION PLAN AND PARALLELISM (agents run concurrently within a wave; each in its own worktree)
Wave 0 (no deps, 4 agents): PPY-78e818, PPY-302a5f, PPY-44a0f9, PPY-e169c5. File overlap: only package.json scripts (REL, CIT). REL and CIT own different workflow files.
Wave 1: PPY-672ea6 (after CIT); PPY-b3a10e and PPY-cddfb8 (after SCH+DER; different files except seed_edition.py helper move: PUB moves helpers, PRT edits seed_article_records: PUB first or coordinate); PPY-39f928 (after REL).
Wave 2: PPY-3e5235, PPY-22a3b4, PPY-1d0f3d (after PUB; three different new modules, share cli.py, graphql_authoring.py INDEX_DEFINITIONS, and the fixture dir procedures/newsroom/tests/fixtures/markus-content: IMP creates it, EXP reuses); PPY-3e5e9d (after PRT+BRD); PPY-085f79, PPY-961956 (after REL+BRD; VID2 after BRD only for site-brand.ts).
Wave 3: PPY-8ef4ca (after LMB); PPY-f00c89 (after PRV+EXP); PPY-e7f81e (after INF).
Wave 4: PPY-ad5ca4 (after UIL+IMP; same components as UIL, never in parallel with it); PPY-fbb1fb (after LMB+INF+STG).
SAME-FILE CONFLICT MAP (serialize or rebase; all are small additive edits unless noted): src/papyrus_content/cli.py (REL lazy videos import, DER, PUB, IMP, EXP, PRT, STG, VID1: each adds a PORTED_COMMANDS entry + dispatch branch + usage line); graphql_authoring.py INDEX_DEFINITIONS and field lists (SCH, PUB, EXP); amplify/data/schema.ts + resource.ts (SCH, LMB, RBP; the two files must always change together); amplify/site-backend.ts and site-backend-config.ts (LMB, RBP); lib/graphql-content-repository.ts (SCH types, PRT, then PRV: real conflict, PRT first); middleware.ts and app/layout.tsx (BRD, then PRV, then STG); lib/site-brand.ts (BRD then VID2); packages/papyrus/scripts/stage.mjs (BRD, INF, VID2); infra/amplify-app-shell/lib/amplify-app-shell.ts (INF then OIC); components/newsroom-article-editor.tsx and markus-ir-preview.tsx (UIL then UIM); scripts/test-theme-packs.cjs and test-anth-us-brand.cjs (CIT then BRD); seed_edition.py (PUB helper move, PRT); package.json scripts (trivial).

DECISIONS MADE IN THE PLAN (so implementers do not ask)
1. Phase 2 follows docs/standard-site.md (Python CLI/Lambdas + papyrus-newsroom) but keeps new Python logic small and fixture-driven so the TypeScript port can take it over (see question 1).
2. Item is edited in place; versionNumber increments per PUBLISH; PublishedItem id = published-<lineageId> (one row per lineage, slug index stays unique). No per-version Item rows yet.
3. Article body storage: bodyMarkus = body only (verbatim, so import->export is byte-identical for canonical files); front matter (incl. CSL-JSON citations) is kept as the raw YAML string in metadata.frontMatterYaml and Item columns (title, deck, byline, publishedAt) are DERIVED from it. bodyIr is an envelope {schemaVersion, markus, document (markus ast IR v1), papyrus {images, citations, citationLists, entries, bibliography}} produced only by derive_body, capped at 300 KB.
4. All body writes go through one Python module (publishing.py): CLI directly, editor through the content-actions Lambda. The browser never parses Markus.
5. Drafts for staging are read from the same Item rows with the same normalizers as PublishedItem (no TypeScript projectItemToPublished); drafts mode is uncached and refuses to start unless SITE_ENV=staging.
6. Static staging = prebuilt site in the private preview/ S3 prefix, served by a gated Next route using the viewer's own Cognito-identity S3 read permission (enforced by AWS, no compute-role bucket policy puzzle, no public bucket).
7. Rebuild-on-publish uses IAM amplify:StartJob from the backend Lambda, not an Amplify webhook (webhook URLs are bearer secrets; decision 7 forbids long-lived tokens).
8. The importer takes a Markus content DIRECTORY. Anth.us (MDX in anthus-site-content) goes through its existing normalizer into web/staging first (Phase 3 passes that dir plus an aliases JSON generated from custom-rules.json). Reader-owned assets (JS/CSS/HTML) stay in the publication repo; only images are CMS media.
9. First release number is whatever Semantic Release picks (1.0.0-next.1); no hand tagging. Infra stays inside @anthusai/papyrus (the 990 MB infra install is accepted, YAGNI).
10. TS ampx seed stops seeding articles (it cannot derive IR); use `papyrus content seed-edition`.

BIGGEST RISKS
1. Language direction conflict (question 1): Markus parsing exists only in Python (anthus-markus); a TS-first Phase 2 would have to port it before bodyIr, publish, importer or editor validation can exist.
2. bodyIr size vs DynamoDB's 400 KB item limit for long articles (Anth.us has 232 images and 197 citations across its posts and solutions): DER measures real content; the fallback (IR in an S3 attachment via the existing model-attachments mechanism) is a follow-up, not built.
3. Amplify repo connection for CDK-created apps without a repo, and branches created before the connection, is only evidenced by the Anth.us console precedent; the staging branch building against another branch's backend (ampx generate outputs) was only simulated locally in the spike. INF includes a scratch-site proof step with Ryan.
4. Production ordering without shims: p.apyr.us has body[] only. Deploy SCH to production, run convert-bodies (dry-run first, Ryan approves), only then promote the reader change (PRT) to main.
5. First-publish mechanics: npm needs the package to exist before a trusted publisher can be attached (one-time placeholder publish by Ryan); semantic-release may refuse a develop prerelease until main has a release.
6. VideoML (VID1/VID2) is the least certain estimate: TI main's pipeline has outgrown Papyrus's copy and needs real merging; end-to-end render cannot run in CI.

QUESTIONS FOR RYAN (short)
1. Language: PPY-1f1489 comment 4174c5 (16:34) said Papyrus is being ported to TypeScript and supersedes papyrus-newsroom/PyPI/Python Lambdas, but PR #99 (merged 16:43) and the restarted spike kept the two-package shape. This plan assumes the merged doc. Confirm, or say that Phase 2 should wait for/port to TS (it changes DER, PUB, IMP, EXP, LMB, REL).
2. Before PPY-78e818 can publish: do the npm placeholder publish + trusted publisher setup and the PyPI pending publisher (exact steps are in the ticket).
3. Approval gate for production: running convert-bodies on p.apyr.us and promoting PRT to main.
4. Pretext index pages list items through editions, so CMS-authored articles outside an edition show at /articles/<slug> but not on the index; decide in Phase 4 whether the blog index lists by recency.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Confirmed 2026-10-05 by Ryan: Papyrus is NOT being ported to TypeScript (that is Chatticus). The plan stands as written (Python + TypeScript, two packages). Epic comment 4174c5 is retracted.

comments.author: home
comments.text: RELEASE GATE (orchestrator, 2026-10-05): once PRT (PPY-cddfb8, PR #109) is on develop, the Pretext reader REQUIRES bodyIr on every item and throws without it. p.apyr.us and newsroom.pilobol.us (and TI) build from Papyrus main and their data has body[] only. DO NOT release develop -> main (or let any site update to a Papyrus version containing PRT) until, per site: (1) the SCH schema is deployed to that site's backend, (2) 'papyrus content convert-bodies' has been run with --apply against that site's backend after a reviewed dry run, (3) the result is verified in a browser. Merging PRT into develop is safe (develop is not deployed).

comments.author: home
comments.text: RELEASE GATE addendum (BRD, PR #114): after BRD reaches main, PAPYRUS_SITE_BRAND must be an EXACT registered id (aliases removed; unknown ids throw at startup): p.apyr.us unset/papyrus OK; newsroom.pilobol.us must be exactly 'pilobol-us' (it is today); Threat Intelligence exactly 'threat-intelligence'; anth.us exactly 'anth-us'. The ?brand= cookie override is gone. Verify each production app's env var BEFORE promoting develop to main. This is in addition to the convert-bodies gate for PRT (#109).

comments.author: home
comments.text: RELEASE GATE addendum (PRV, PR #119): middleware.ts now declares runtime 'nodejs' for ALL sites (needed for fs via getAmplifyServerRuntime). Not verified on Amplify WEB_COMPUTE. Before promoting develop -> main: deploy a build with this middleware to a non-production Amplify branch/app and confirm pages, the /newsroom redirect and robots.txt work, and that production-mode behaviour is unchanged (no gate, no banner, no noindex). Also still unproven against a real backend: staging-auth-test.mjs (editor/non-editor/anonymous) and the content-actions Lambda (LMB #116): both need one scratch sandbox proof (AWS SSO login by Ryan).
